agreements.title: COURTESY CALL ON YB DATHE Taro Kono, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan called on YB Dato’ Saifuddin Abdullah, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Malaysia on 11 July 2018 at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs during his working visit to Malaysia from 10 to 11 July 2018. This was HE Kono’s first visit to Malaysia since his appointment as Foreign Minister in August 2017 and the first meeting between the two Ministers. HE Kono is also the first Foreign Minister to pay a courtesy call on YB Foreign Minister. YB Foreign Minister expressed his deepest condolences to HE Kono over the flash floods and landslides due to heavy rains in western Japan. The incident affecting areas in Hiroshima, Osaka, Shiga, Hyogo, Okayama, Kyoto and Fukuoka has caused deaths of more than 100 people while many are still missing. Both Ministers were pleased with the current state of bilateral relations and agreed to continue strengthening and fostering greater cooperation in many areas. Malaysia and Japan have agreed to elevate the relationship from an Enhanced Partnership to a Strategic Partnership in 2015. Both Ministers followed up on the proposals and decisions made during the meeting between the two Prime Ministers, YAB Tun Dr. Mahathir Mohamad and HE Shinzo Abe on 12 June 2018 in Tokyo, Japan. They discussed matters related to the rejuvenation and further enhancement of the Look East Policy which would benefit both countries especially through education and human resource development; optimize the utilization of the railway line where Japan and Malaysia have agreed to look into ways to increase the efficiency of Malaysia’s existing railway lines; consideration on soft credit assistance as well as maritime cooperation, where Japan has assisted through the contribution of two patrol vessels and assistance in human capacity development. Both Ministers also discussed matters related to the regional developments. On the situation in the Korean Peninsula, both Ministers welcomed the development of efforts for the denuclearization, and concurred that both sides should remain committed to implement all sanctions as stipulated under the United Nations Security Council resolutions. On the developments in the South China Sea, both Ministers agreed on the importance of the sea lines of communication and maintaining peace in the South China Sea. Both Ministers also agreed for ASEAN to play leading and active role in managing the situation and conflicts in the South China Sea. They also exchanged ideas on how to promote regional peace and security in the region. On the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for the Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), Japan has mentioned that its Chief Negotiator for CPTPP will be coming to Malaysia to explain the current arrangement of the Agreement to the Government of Malaysia. HE Kono looked forward to working with YB Foreign Minister both bilaterally and in multilateral platforms including the ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting which will take place in Singapore in early August and the United Nations General Assembly in New York in September. The Courtesy Call provided not only an avenue for both Ministers to meet for the first time but also an opportunity for both sides to share and exchange views on issues of mutual interest. PUTRAJAYA 11 July 2018O’ SAIFUDDIN ABDULLAH MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF MALAYSIA BY HIS EXCELLENCY TARO KONO MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF JAPAN 11 JULY 2018
